maria_p: FYI — EDU pilot (small cluster of universities) just asked for an exemption: unlimited burst credits for the first 6 weeks, custom SLA (99.9) and a clause to roll back to normal tier after pilot. They framed it as 'critical for adoption'.
aj: ugh. unlimited for 6 weeks is risky. we need clear guardrails (telemetry + kill-switch). is this a paid pilot or free?
maria_p: paid, but minimal committed $ (introductory discount). CTO ok to consider pilot-level terms if we can make it a defined add-on that auto-terminates.
kevin_r: product POV — we can ship a "pilot surge" add-on: timeboxed, telemetry gated, capable of central disable. Mechanically: allocate a temporary burst pool per-customer with soft-limit warnings and hard kill at 120% of declared pilot capacity.
siobhan: what's the difference between soft-limit and hard kill in contract terms? legal will push back on anything that looks like "unlimited".
legal-bot: draft clause suggestion: \n\n"Pilot Surge Addendum: Provider will enable a time-limited surge allocation for Customer during the Pilot Period (Start Date — End Date). Provider will monitor usage and may impose automated throttles if usage exceeds 120% of agreed pilot allocation to protect platform stability. Provider will notify Customer 24 hours before hard throttling. No refunds will be issued for throttled usage during an escalated event caused by misuse or abuse."\n\nlegal-bot: happy to iterate. we can't promise SLA improvements (99.9) unless we reserve dedicated capacity or add a penalty clause.
emma_fin: finance — small committed $ means we shouldn't eat too much marginal cost. we need explicit per-token surcharge for pilot surge beyond X tokens. otherwise unit economics blow up.
nathan_ops: ops: we need a rollout path. prefer using existing dedicated pool machinery with a tagging layer. also require a manual/automated kill-switch in console with audit log. can we require a pre-signed PO and spike contact?
aj: requirement checklist: 1) timebox window, 2) telemetry gating thresholds + alerts, 3) explicit pilot allocation in contract, 4) surcharge for overage, 5) kill switch + ops playbook, 6) legal addendum draft, 7) launch criteria (smoke tests + canary).
kevin_r: UX question — product needs a visible banner in console when pilot surge active and a per-route rate view. Also a single-click terminate for support + ops.
siobhan: for launch criteria let's add: no regressions in latency under pilot load testing, cost guardrails in place, internal alerting to product/ops/finance on day 1, and agreement on rollback plan.
maria_p: agreed. question for the group: should this be an add-on SKU (pilot-surge) that later maps to Priority Lane or a one-off contract clause per customer? Pros/cons?
emma_fin: SKU is better for repeatability + pricing integrity. one-off clauses create exceptions that sales will ask to replicate for others. SKU enables standard surcharge and telemetry hooks.
legal-bot: SKU + standard addendum is easier for scaling. we'll craft a templated addendum with variables: pilot window, declared allocation, surcharge rate, notification window, kill-switch ops steps.
nathan_ops: tech constraints: tagging + quota enforcement should be doable in 2 sprints if scoped tightly. need eng runtime to expose allocation TTL and a hook for automated throttle.
aj: engineering ask: can runtime guarantee a throttle path that doesn't propagate errors to caller (e.g., 429 with clear error body)? we need graceful degradation to return structured 429 + 'pilot-throttled' code.
kevin_r: yes, that's acceptable. product will standardize error schema and update SDK docs.
siobhan: timeline proposal: draft addendum + SKU pricing by EOW, ops/eng spike next week (2 sprints), legal sign-off + pilot contract next-week+1. target pilot launch in 4 weeks.
maria_p: selling point to EDU customers: "time-limited pilot surge to evaluate scale" + clear conversion path to paid Priority/Reserved tiers. keep comms tight.
emma_fin: add a retention metric piece: if pilot usage converts to paid within 12 weeks we'll credit some of the surcharge back (promo credit). make it a one-time credit to encourage conversion.
legal-bot: we can add that as a conditional credit clause. will draft with finite language.
aj: outstanding concerns?
kevin_r: just engineering capacity — label as P1 for runtime spike, but flag we need no scope creep.
siobhan: sales enablement doc needed: 2-paragraph explainer + contract checklist + ops contact list.
maria_p: assigning actions: legal-bot -> draft template addendum; emma_fin -> propose surcharge bands; nathan_ops -> ops playbook + kill-switch design; kevin_r -> runtime spike ticket; aj -> vendor/sales constraints liaison. we'll reconvene Tues 9am. :thumbsup:
